title: What a commit really records
summary: Explains that a commit is a snapshot of tracked files with an author, a time, a message and a parent, and how the staging area lets you build a commit on purpose.

title: Branches are just names
summary: A branch is a movable label on a commit, and HEAD is the pointer that says where you are. Compares a fast-forward merge with a merge commit that has two parents.

title: branches are just names
summary: A short note on branches and HEAD, written as a quick mirror of the longer guide.

title: Conflicts and undo: a field guide
summary: Covers what happens when a merge conflict stops, how to read the conflict markers, and the differences between restore, revert and reset.

title: Sharing work: fetch, pull and push
summary: Explains what a remote and a remote-tracking branch are, and compares fetch, pull and push.

title: Quick cheat sheet: sending and getting changes
summary: A short guide to sending and getting changes for people who want the short version, written before fetch and pull were compared carefully in a longer guide.

title: A tidy commit routine
summary: Covers staging chosen changes on purpose, writing a clear commit message, and fixing the most recent commit when needed.

title: The best graphical Git clients, ranked
summary: Compares desktop applications for people who prefer a visual interface over the command line, with picks for a top choice, a runner-up and a budget option.

title: Distributed version control before Git: a 1998 retrospective
summary: Looks back at older, centralized source-code workflows from a paper archive, from before distributed source tools became common; no mention of the ideas covered in this program.
